title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Paul's scope: evils from first Adam, goods from second
pass_a_gloss: For Paul's aim is to teach what evils flowed from the first Adam, and what goods by contrast from the second, into the human race—so we see it is no wonder that, when one man was so powerful to ruin us, one man, Jesus Christ, can save us. So he carefully compares goods from this one with evils from that. Who then believes he meant to pass in silence that evil which both derives from Adam into us and is the cause of all our sins?
pass_b_english: For the Apostle's aim is to teach what evils from the first Adam, what goods by contrast from the second Adam, flowed into the human race, so that we may understand it is not wonderful, when one man was so powerful to destroy us, that one man, Jesus Christ, can save us. And so he accurately compares the goods proceeded from this one into us with the evils proceeded from that one. Who therefore would believe that he wished to pass over in silence that evil which it is agreed both is derived from Adam into us, and is the cause of all our sins?
source_text: Scopus enim Apostoli est docere quae mala a primo Adamo, quae contra bona a secundo Adamo in genus humanum fluxerint, ut intelligamus mirum non esse, cum unus homo ad nos perdendos tam potens fuerit, unum hominem, Iesum Christum, nos posse servare. Itaque bona ab hoc in nos profecta malis ab illo profectis accurate comparat. Quis igitur credat eum voluisse id malum silentio praeterire, quod constat & ex Adamo in nos derivari, & causam omnium nostrorum peccatorum esse?

choices.choice: Paul compares first-Adam evils with second-Adam goods
